glass.note: Translucent counterpart to Surface, used on app-chrome cards over the fixed map layer with backdrop-filter blur. Overlay color; no tonal ramp.

glass-raised.note: Translucent counterpart to Surface Raised, used on the nav bar and the how-to modal. Overlay color; no tonal ramp.

glass-line.note: Translucent counterpart to Line, for hairline/dashed borders on glass surfaces. Overlay color; no tonal ramp.

map-line.note: The background rail-map route line. Deliberately near-invisible. Overlay color; no tonal ramp.

map-line-faint.note: The background rail-map graticule/coastline linework. Overlay color; no tonal ramp.

map-dot.note: The background rail-map city-label text color. Overlay color; no tonal ramp.

masthead.purpose: The arrival-city line of the h1 route lockup (36px) - the single largest, boldest text in the app.

display.purpose: Reserved large-headline step; unused now that the route title runs at Masthead scale.

title.purpose: Route codes and city-pair headers, set in mono at display scale.

body.purpose: Descriptions, notes, and form input text.

label.purpose: Pill buttons, status flags, nav labels, badges, field labels - anything functional or code-like.

shadows.name: ambient-app
shadows.purpose: Dark app-shell cards (day-card, check-item) - reads as part of the app, not an object.

shadows.name: lifted-document
shadows.purpose: Journey (inter-city train) cards - reads as a physical ticket resting on the screen.

shadows.name: lifted-document-light
shadows.purpose: Local-transit flight-cards - the lighter variant of the paper-card lift.

motion.name: route-transition
motion.purpose: Route-timeline plane icon sliding to the trip's current progress position.

motion.name: toggle-transition
motion.value: border-color .15s ease, background .15s ease, color .15s ease
motion.purpose: Nearby-search toggle buttons switching to their active tinted state.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one solid-amber call-to-action pill per row (BOOK, ADD, SAVE, the Eurail app CTA).

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: A same-row secondary action next to a primary pill (FROM STAY, TO STAY) - transparent with amber text, same shape as the primary pill.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 600; padding: 6px 10px; border-radius: 16px; border: none; background: transparent; color: #E3A542; cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color: #F1C170; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #E3A542; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Icon Button

components.name: App Shell Card

Eiffel Tower + Seine cruise

components.name: Stamp Badge
components.description: Signature component: a dashed-border circle rotated -6deg showing a day's date, colored by that day's city - the strongest expression of the ink-stamp metaphor.

components.name: Day Timeline
components.description: A day's activities as rows on a small vertical rail (a per-day miniature of the header's own route-line motif) instead of stacked cards or a flat divided list - a hollow amber-ringed node per stop on a continuous line, indented text with a clear name/description weight step.

narrative.overview: The app is a dark, after-dark travel-app shell that holds physical travel documents inside it. Everything native to the app itself (the itinerary days, the packing checklist, the tab bar) lives in flat navy surfaces, as if you're looking at a phone screen on a night train. Everything that represents a real booked or bookable object (a train leg, a local-transit info card) is rendered as a warm cream-paper card with ink-colored text, dropped onto that dark shell with a pronounced shadow, as if a paper ticket or boarding pass were physically lying on top of the glass. The two-tone contrast between "app chrome" and "paper document" is the single organizing idea; nothing else in the system competes with it. Monospace type (IBM Plex Mono) is used everywhere something reads like it was printed by a ticket machine: route codes, dates, status flags, nav labels, pill buttons. A geometric display face (Space Grotesk) carries headlines and titles. Circular ink-stamp badges, dashed cut-lines, and punched-notch cutouts on ticket cards complete the passport-and-boarding-pass vocabulary. Nothing in the system is decorative for its own sake; every recurring motif (dashes, notches, stamps) directly references a physical travel-document detail.
keyCharacteristics: Dark navy app shell vs. warm cream-paper document cards, always ink-on-paper / cream-on-navy, never mixed
Monospace for anything ticket-like (codes, dates, statuses, labels); a display face only for headlines/titles
Dashed borders and circular notch cutouts standing in for perforation and stamps
One accent (amber) reserved for primary action and current state; a small red/green/amber status vocabulary for booking urgency
Six named per-city hues used only as wayfinding accents (day-card left border, route dots), never as UI chrome

A vintage rail-map (route Amsterdam→Paris→Interlaken→Vienna→Budapest→Rome) absolutely positioned with main's own scrolling content as its containing block, layered behind every tab's rows - it moves through the exact same coordinate system as the content on top of it (drag the checklist, the map moves the same pixel amount), deliberately not viewport-pinned after fixed/absolute-to-body variants proved unreliable on real iOS/WebKit
An asymmetric 'ticket-stub' corner radius (one sharp corner, one rounded) on primary content cards and primary buttons, paired with a plain text-link style (no fill/border) for secondary actions

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Amber is the only color used for a primary call-to-action or an active/selected control. Teal, the status colors, and the city colors are all narrowly scoped to one specific job each and never substitute for amber.

rules.name: The Paper-or-Navy Rule
rules.body: A card is either a paper-document card (paper background, ink text, warm-toned shadow) or an app-shell card (surface background, cream text, cool ambient shadow). The two never blend on the same element.

rules.name: The Printed-Label Rule
rules.body: Any text that represents a code, date, status, or short machine-legible fact (not a sentence) is set in IBM Plex Mono, regardless of where it appears in the hierarchy. Any text that represents a name, title, or description is set in Space Grotesk or IBM Plex Sans.

rules.name: The Document Lift Rule
rules.body: Only paper-toned cards get a pronounced shadow. A dark-surface card never carries more than the ambient level, no matter its importance.

rules.name: The Perforation Rule
rules.body: Dashed and dotted borders and circular notch cutouts are reserved for elements that represent a physical, tearable, or stampable document, or the rules that separate its internal rows. A purely digital control never borrows this motif for its own sake.

rules.name: The Ticket-Stub Rule
rules.body: The asymmetric one-sharp/one-round corner radius is reserved for elements that represent a torn or issued document/action: primary content cards and primary buttons. A container that isn't standing in for a physical object uses a plain symmetric radius or none.

rules.name: The Single-Scroll Rule
rules.body: .app never scrolls as a document; main is the one internal scroll container (flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto), and .app is a true fixed-height shell (height: 100dvh; overflow: hidden) so it can never grow past the viewport. Header and nav stay visually anchored to the viewport while only main's content moves.

rules.name: The Map Rides With Content Rule
rules.body: The map is position:absolute with main (not body) as its containing block, so it scrolls through the same coordinate system as main's content by construction. Fixed and absolute-to-body variants were tried and both visibly dragged during a real iOS/WebKit touch-scroll gesture - a documented WebKit bug class no GPU-layer hint reliably prevents. main and .panel both carry explicit z-index to keep the map's stacking contained inside main, away from header/nav. Do not reintroduce position:fixed or absolute-to-body for this element.

dos: Do put any code, date, status, or label-length string in IBM Plex Mono; put any name, title, or sentence-length string in Space Grotesk or IBM Plex Sans.
Do keep the paper/navy split absolute: paper background always pairs with ink text and a lifted shadow; navy/surface background always pairs with cream text and an ambient shadow.
Do keep app-chrome surfaces as translucent glass over the fixed map layer, and paper cards fully opaque.
Do reserve the ticket-stub asymmetric radius for primary content cards and primary buttons; use a plain symmetric radius (or none) everywhere else.
Do reserve dashed/dotted borders and circular notches for content that represents a physical, perforated, or stamped document.
Do limit a card's action row to one primary (amber, ticket-stub, solid) action plus text-link/icon secondary actions - never two solid amber buttons side by side.
donts: Don't use amber for anything other than the single primary action or current/active state in a given row or tab.
Don't introduce a fourth type family; the display/body/mono trio covers every case in the system.
Don't give a dark-surface (app-chrome) element the pronounced "lifted" shadow reserved for paper document cards.
Don't use a city color anywhere except the day-card left border, the route-timeline dots, and the background map's own city dots.
Don't let the background map layer become legible enough to read as content, or scroll with the page.
